title: Owner Review Adjudication
heading: Owner review adjudication pipeline
intro: How a blinded pair of NYC landlord sides becomes a SAME, DIFFERENT or INDETERMINATE call. Deterministic record work assembles a neutral panel that a human and an automated adjudicator both read. One model call decides, with a bounded escalation loop and a hard gate. Select any box for what it does, the worked pair P0214, how the agent compares with the human labels, and what is still open.

views.label: Pipeline
views.title: Pipeline overview
views.desc: A blinded pair and the primary records feed deterministic assembly into a dossier, fingerprints, an overlap and busy-office coverage. The resulting panel is read by a human reviewer and by a model call that returns a verdict, with a bounded escalation loop. A verification and hard-gate step produces the final annotation.

views.title: Decision logic for one pair
views.desc: Shared signals are stripped of noise. A substantive shared owner leads toward SAME, with a deed-only gate that can downgrade to INDETERMINATE. Otherwise positive distinctness leads to DIFFERENT, and an open question either escalates or holds at INDETERMINATE. Advisory flags annotate a call without changing it.

pair.title: Blinded pair
pair.lede: Two landlord sides, A and B, each a name plus the building lots (BBLs) attributed to it, handed over with no grouping or label attached.
what: One queue line holds the pair id and, for each side, a reference, a name and its BBLs.
The loader raises an error for any line that carries stratum, signal, watchline, wow, decision, label or anchor. The tool cannot see which system produced a pair.
The agent gets no prior grouping either. Its codebook says to judge only on the records provided.
nums: pairs in the queue
A: MINDY SPOLAN, 1 building. B: MINDY SPOLAN, 1 building.

records.title: Primary records
records.lede: ACRIS conveyances, HPD registrations, PLUTO and NYS DOS filings, read through a read-only connection.
what: The connection is read-only and autocommit, with a statement timeout on the large name searches.

Primary records only. The tools never read the system's own inference tables (landlords_with_connections, CONNECTED_BY_* edges, owner groups), because using the system's output to adjudicate the system is circular.
ACRIS gives the deed chain with parties and amounts, HPD the owner contacts and managing agent, PLUTO the recorded owner and building class, DOS each LLC's principals and process address.

s1.title: 1 · Dossier assembly
s1.lede: Pulls every primary record for each side's buildings and lays them out neutrally: no highlighting of a match, no conclusion.
what: Per side: PLUTO building facts, the full deed chain newest first, and HPD contacts. DOS filings are looked up for every LLC name that appears.
DOS is the one slow lookup (about 5 seconds), so the web app loads it lazily. The agent loads it up front, so DOS principals can feed the shared-name overlap.
By contract the module never imports a matching heuristic from the producing pipeline.
nums: buildings in P0214: 4033240050 on A, 4033240009 on B

s2.title: 2 · Fingerprint
s2.lede: Per-side rollups of who the owners of record, PLUTO owners, HPD principals, DOS principals and managing agents are, deduplicated, counted and role-tagged.
what: The owner of record is the latest deed grantee that is not a bank or lender, so a foreclosure or mortgage deed on top does not read as the owner.
Names are classified against public lists: institutional (City, NYCHA, HDFC and similar), financier and bank. A match is greyed as noise, never excluded.
Each name's roles are recorded (head officer, corp owner, individual owner, joint owner, officer, shareholder, owner of record, PLUTO owner, DOS principal), with the business addresses it uses.
A side is a resident co-op or condo portfolio when at least half its buildings are marked that way in HPD contacts.
nums: A
no deed grantee on record; PLUTO owner MJB HOLDING CORP
B
owner of record and PLUTO owner AUDLEY STREET REALTY LLC
open: SiteManager contacts are not used as principals, and a DOS name counts as a person only if it has two to four words and no corporate term.
A deed attached to the wrong lot by ACRIS (a conflation) would become a false owner of record. This is a known, deferred case (P0085).

s3.title: 3 · Overlap
s3.lede: The cross-side signals the codebook keys on: shared names, agents, addresses and deeds, with the noise already flagged.
what: Shared names are exact after normalization, plus fuzzy person-name matches: reversed 'Last, First' order, and dropped middle names, initials or typos when a shared business address confirms the person.
Each shared name carries address_match: true (the address confirms one person), false (addresses differ, a namesake risk) or null (a side has no address).
Shared agents are kept apart because they are management. Shared deeds carry stale, nominal, mega, bank and financier flags, and the clean subset is the substantive deeds.
Role structure is computed: a shared head officer is an owner-operator link even at a busy office, disjoint head officers point to management, and a shared shareholder is a shared equity owner.
nums: shared name: a head officer on both sides, sole on each, with different addresses (address_match false)
shared managing agent: IMPERIAL CONSULTING GROUP
shared addresses, and 0 shared deeds
open: address_match compares business addresses. An owner who registers each building at its own address gets false by design, which own_building_addresses marks.
Shared agents match on normalized names only, so one firm spelled two ways goes unmatched.

s4.title: 4 · Busy-office coverage
s4.lede: Quantifies each shared address and managing agent citywide, so a management hub is not read as a shared owner.
what: For a shared business address: the distinct buildings and distinct head officers registered there. Five or more head officers marks it busy.
For a shared agent: the buildings it registers on, for context. An agent is busy by nature, so it is not itself flagged.
A shared name confirmed only at a busy address gets address_match_office_busy: the match is management co-occurrence, not a shared owner.
nums: buildings IMPERIAL CONSULTING GROUP registers on, citywide (the two in this pair)
open: Addresses are matched as strings, so one office written two ways counts as two addresses and the hub is under-counted.

s5.title: 5 · The panel
s5.lede: The neutral dossier plus the overlap, serialized into what a reviewer sees. The human reads it in the web app, and the agent reads the same structure.
what: The context starts with a note explaining the overlap fields, then the overlap, then each side's records. Deeds are trimmed to the most recent six per building and BBLs to 40.
The renderer never emits a label, a score or a prior grouping.
Whatever the fingerprint drops is absent here, and a reviewer cannot weigh what the panel does not show.

human.title: Human reviewer
human.lede: A person reads the panel in a web app and submits an annotation: label, evidence tiers, the deed checks and a rationale.
what: Annotations go to an append-only SQLite store. The latest row per pair and annotator wins at export.
The human's labels are the gold the agent is scored against. The agent is one more annotator, agent-sonnet-v1, in the same format and never merged into the gold.
The web app applies the same hard gate when a SAME is submitted.
nums: human labels, SAME / DIFFERENT / INDETERMINATE, on 512 pairs
open: The gold is one person's labels.

s6.title: 6 · Adjudicate
s6.lede: One model call reads the panel and returns a structured Verdict: the label, the evidence tiers it rests on, grounded evidence items, and whether it is resolved.
what: The system prompt is the reviewer codebook. A shared owner or principal is the deciding axis, a shared managing agent is management and not ownership, and a shared address counts only if the owners match.
Evidence tiers: T1 a deed, T2 a DOS filing, T3 a shared HPD principal, T4 an outside record from the web. A shared name alone or an address alone is not a tier.
Every claim is quoted as a record value with its source (panel, tool:name or web). The rationale only summarizes those items.
The verdict sets resolved and, when false, the evidence gap to fill.
nums: SAME
P0214: tier T3, resolved on the first call
grounded evidence items, all sourced from the panel
for the call, with claude-sonnet-5
measured: Against the human labels on all 512 pairs: 483 agree (94.3%). SAME recall 95.5% and precision 97.7%; DIFFERENT recall 93.5% and precision 96.2%. The agent returned INDETERMINATE 15 times, the human twice.
The baseline run of 2026-10-01 took about 100 minutes and about $16.
open: The disagreements: 6 false SAMEs and 8 missed SAMEs, plus 14 cases where the agent held at INDETERMINATE and the human committed. The main families are a shared officer or agent at a hub read as ownership, a shared individual owner discounted as management, and namesake or spelling-variant resolution in both directions.
The codebook and signals were tuned on cases from this same queue (P0147, P0214, P0390 and others appear in the code's comments), so the agreement is not an out-of-sample estimate.
After the role-structure change, a 12-pair rerun of earlier errors matched the human on 9, against 8 for the baseline. P0212 and P0390 are still false SAMEs and P0363 is still missed.

s7.title: 7 · Escalate
s7.lede: When the verdict is not resolved, the model calls curated tools to fill the named evidence gap, then returns to adjudication with what it found.
what: Tools are primary-records only: the deed chain, HPD contacts and PLUTO facts for a BBL, DOS by entity, a party's other ACRIS deeds, the LLCs a person is a principal of, and web search (tier T4).
principal_crosscheck is bound to the pair and computes in code whether a person's footprint ties both sides, so the model does not infer it from raw rows.
At most 2 rounds. If a round makes no tool call, that is recorded and the verdict stands.
nums: escalations on P0214: resolved on the first pass
measured: 28 of the 507 pairs that completed in the first baseline pass escalated.
open: Some identity questions need data the tools cannot reach. DOS lookups cover active filings only, and a missing CEO is not evidence that two entities are unrelated (the tool's own note).

s8.title: 8 · Verify + hard gate
s8.lede: Flag-only faithfulness checks, then one hard gate, then a schema-conformant annotation.
what: verify_evidence checks every evidence value against the source it claims: panel values against the serialized dossier, tool and web values against what was gathered. A value is grounded when at least 80% of its significant tokens appear.
The hard gate downgrades a SAME that rests on a deed alone (tiers equal to T1) to INDETERMINATE unless all three deed checks hold.
Two structural flags can fire on a SAME, t3_not_address_confirmed and coop_condo_management. Flags never change the label.
The annotation matches the output schema exactly, and agent-only fields go to a sidecar meta record.
nums: flag on P0214: t3_not_address_confirmed, advisory
label changes by the gate
measured: In the baseline run, the gate downgraded 5 deed-only calls to INDETERMINATE (P0037, P0074, P0112 and P0417 among them), which prevented false SAMEs but stopped short of DIFFERENT. The run raised 30 t3_not_address_confirmed flags and 1 coop_condo_management flag.
open: The address flag is advisory on purpose. A hard gate there would downgrade real same-owner pairs such as P0214, whose per-building addresses differ.
49 panel-sourced values were flagged as not found. That check compares tokens, so treat a flag as a prompt to look, not proof of fabrication.

outcome.title: Annotation
outcome.lede: One of three labels, scored against the human gold exactly like a human line, with agent-only fields kept in a sidecar.
what: SAME, DIFFERENT or INDETERMINATE, plus the tiers, the deed checks on a SAME, a severe flag on a DIFFERENT, and the rationale.
INDETERMINATE is a first-class answer, used when the record cannot settle it.
The store is append-only, so a correction never erases the trail.
nums: SAME
P0214: the agent and the human agree
measured: Agent labels on 512 pairs: 259 SAME, 238 DIFFERENT, 15 INDETERMINATE.
open: The two annotators can diverge, and the agent is judged against the human's reviewed labels.

v-signals.title: Shared signals
v-signals.lede: Everything the two sides have in common, ranked by what it means for ownership.
what: A shared owner or principal (an owner-role person, or a shared conveyance deed) is the deciding axis. A sole shared owner on both sides is strongest.
A shared managing agent is management. It points DIFFERENT and never by itself makes two landlords the same owner.
A shared business address is ownership evidence only if the owners also match. Alone it is a busy-office hint.
A shared name alone, or an address alone, is a hint and not a tier.
nums: signals in the overlap for P0214: a shared head officer and a shared managing agent. A shared DOS process address shows up in the DOS filings.

v-discount.title: Discount the noise
v-discount.lede: Computed flags strip co-occurrence noise so only real same-owner evidence remains.
what: Institutional and financier names (City, NYCHA, HDFC, banks) are shared because they touch everything.
A busy office (five or more head officers) links unrelated owners, and a shared name confirmed only there is flagged.
A co-op or condo officer is a board member or managing agent, which is management.
Stale (superseded), nominal, mega and bank deeds do not count as substantive bridges.

v-owner.title: Substantive shared owner?
v-owner.lede: Is there a surviving shared owner of record, an address-confirmed principal, or a current co-conveyance deed?
what: Yes on any of these: the same owning entity on both sides, a shared principal confirmed by a coinciding non-busy address, a DOS tie or a second co-appearing principal, or a substantive shared deed.
Same owner is not the same person: two partners, or two front LLCs one controller re-deeded a block into, are SAME.
A shared principal behind two different corporate owners is possible common control, so it is not evidence of distinctness. The model escalates or holds.
nums: SAME
P0214: the address test failed, and the call rested on a sole shared head officer plus the managing agent, a shared DOS process address and the deed chain

v-gate.title: Deed alone? Three checks
v-gate.lede: A SAME resting on a lone deed is accepted only if all three deed checks hold. Otherwise it becomes INDETERMINATE.
what: The checks: entity_identity (the linking party is the same entity, not a name collision), successor_reality (each successor is a single-purpose shell), restructuring_not_sale (a related-party transfer, not an arm's-length sale).
It applies only when the tiers equal T1. A SAME that also rests on a principal passes through.
It is the one place a label is changed mechanically. It is signal-agnostic and unit-tested.
measured: 5 deed-only calls were downgraded in the baseline run.

v-diff.title: Positive distinctness?
v-diff.lede: DIFFERENT needs positive evidence of distinct owners, not merely that no link was found.
what: Distinct grantees, distinct principals and no linking conveyance count. A shared managing agent, a busy-office address or a family office is management, which supports DIFFERENT once the owners themselves differ.
On a DIFFERENT, severe is true when conflating the sides would be a consequential mis-attribution, for example when one side has a large footprint.
Absence of a link on a PLUTO-only side is not distinctness. The model prefers INDETERMINATE.

v-escalate.title: Could a lookup settle it?
v-escalate.lede: An open call either escalates for the specific missing evidence or, if nothing more would help, holds at INDETERMINATE.
what: Before resting on DIFFERENT, the model checks it is not absence of a link: a shared owner-role principal, a distinctive shared name or a shared non-busy office with no confirming deed or DOS filing is a gap to escalate.
The route is code: escalate while resolved is false and fewer than 2 rounds have run, otherwise finalize.

v-same-out.title: SAME
v-same-out.lede: The records show the same beneficial owner.
what: It rests on a shared owner or principal, or a linking deed. A deed-only SAME has passed the three checks.
It carries the deed checks when it rests on T1.
measured: The agent's SAME calls matched the human label 253 times out of 259 (97.7%).

v-indet-out.title: INDETERMINATE
v-indet-out.lede: The record cannot settle it. It is a first-class answer, not a cop-out.
what: A PLUTO-only side, a lone address-unconfirmed principal, or an unresolved identity all land here.
It is also where a gated deed-only SAME ends up.
measured: The agent returned INDETERMINATE 15 times on 512 pairs, the human 2 times.
open: The agent holds more often than the human commits. Ten of its holds were pairs the human called DIFFERENT.

v-diff-out.title: DIFFERENT
v-diff-out.lede: The records show genuinely distinct owners.
what: Positive distinctness, not absence of a link.
The severe flag marks consequential conflation.
measured: The agent's DIFFERENT calls matched the human label 229 times out of 238 (96.2%).

v-flags.title: Advisory flags
v-flags.lede: Faithfulness and risk flags surfaced for the reviewer. They annotate a call and never change its label.
what: t3_not_address_confirmed: a SAME resting on a shared principal whose addresses do not coincide, with none confirmed (namesake risk).
coop_condo_management: a SAME resting only on an officer link between two resident co-op or condo portfolios.
unsupported panel, tool or web claim: an evidence value the verifier could not find in its cited source.
measured: Baseline run: 30 t3_not_address_confirmed, 1 coop_condo_management, 49 unsupported panel claims.
open: Flags are advisory by design. Gating the address flag would downgrade genuine same-owner pairs confirmed by other signals.
